question: India's National Deworming Day programme recommends single-dose albendazole (400 mg for children ≥2 years) twice yearly for soil-transmitted helminthiasis in school-age children.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This is TRUE. The National Deworming Day (NDD) programme gives albendazole 400 mg as a single dose to children ≥2 years (200 mg for 1–2 years) twice yearly. This targets all three major soil-transmitted helminths: Ascaris lumbricoides, Trichuris trichiura, and hookworm. Albendazole is the preferred agent over mebendazole for these conditions.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. The National Deworming Day (NDD) programme under the Ministry of Health administers single-dose albendazole 400 mg to all children aged 1–19 years twice yearly (biannual). Children 1–2 years receive 200 mg. This mass drug administration targets Ascaris, Trichuris, and hookworm simultaneously. Albendazole is the drug of choice for all three major soil-transmitted helminths.
